I'm not sure why there are more than a handful negative reviews, if anything, I really enjoyed playing this game and I think it totally worth the price. I honestly had doubts before pushing the "buy" button when I read the mixed reviews, I wasn't sure if this would be good enough, granted that impulse purchasing has always failed me one way or another, but boy- aren't I glad I YOLO'd this. I guess it's part of the gamble, huh?
As mentioned by other reviews, this game is played out just like Old Maid and your goal is to fool your opponents by playing your cards right, per se. All the cards were designed to symbolize the 7 sins (Pride, Wrath, Gluttony, Sloth, Lust, Envy, Greed), which sort of foreshadows the characters in a way. Alongside with an extra "Lamia Card", basically the Joker that you need to get rid of, if you ever find one landing on your hands. You have Suspic/Doubt (pretend to be suspicious), Nervo/Nervou (pretend to be nervous), Grin (literally), 3 reactions to trick your opponents into picking the Lamia Card, which is only available if you got one on your hands. It was quite easy at first, as soon as I found the pattern it was a breeze rushing through the chapters. At the later on chapters though, namely the last few rounds took me one or two tries to get through, because the opponents stopped reacting the way I thought they would and their poker faces fooled me quite a few times.
I'm not a fan of card games, but this game definitely takes the cake out of all the others I've played. The story was told in such a way that resembles the Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors series and Sweet Fuse ~By Your Side~ (And especially the anime, Death Parade!). It gave off of this feeling that left me crossing my fingers and panicked whenever I failed to trick the others. It engaged me into feeling like I was in that room, playing by Lamia's rules, and that I had to do my best to help The Player (The main character) to escape this madness.
At most times, I don't appreciate open ended games with incomplete story, I guess that's just my preference. This game had exactly that, it dropped hints here and there, sometimes an important piece of information could be found in dialogues, and at other times, it was those obvious evidences that were left behind by the previous round's losers. The game expects the player to gather up information, organize them and conclude them on our own. Granted, the game does lack on the delivery aspect, as most often than not, it expected a lot out of the player to have a good understanding of the plot, while init of itself isn't as clear as day. If you so desire to throw on your wool coat and whip out your thinking hat to play detective, then this game would prove to be quite enjoyable, at least by my standards. Although in the end, the game didn't explain everything exactly, even when the situation was understood, because of how enjoyable the game was, I anticipated for a sequel (or a prequel) to this (soon to be made?) series.

I got this in a Visual Novel bundle and figured to get a good entertainment and easy 100%. Plus, it had trading cards to sell.
What I got is not what I was looking for. As written in the other reviews, it is not a VN, but a simple card game based on luck.

On a technical note, the game has a little reaction delay: where Ren'Py VNs react instantaneously on mouse clicks, this game takes a fraction of a second before it reacts. It's not much, but it's there and enough to annoy me.
On a 4:3 or 5:4 resolution, you cannot run the game in fullscreen without the graphics being stretched vertically - even although it is done in Unity, which allows extensive resolution configuration.
Apparently, this game only comes with 64 bit support. Seriously? There's NOTHING in the whole game that requires a 64 bit CPU. Even an old (32 bit) 500 MHz machine should be able to handle what is presented here. I can only speculate what might be the cause of this. Most likely, it's bad design.
For me, this seems like a quick cash grab.
Avoid. Even that cheap, you can do better.

The Binding of Isaac is a hack n slash flash game at its core. It may not bring change to its genre. But that doesn't mean it is not fun, for a simplistic game it has rather interesting storyline and gameplay. You play as one of six unlockable characters traveling through room after room, killing the monsters that dwell within the confinements of the many rooms. Eventually, you will face the ultimate boss which happens to be your mom. The difficulty cranks up slightly as you travel deeper in the floors, each floor has a unique boss and treasure room to make your character stronger. On the topic of treasure, the game has many items which makes each game feel new with different combinations of items. Well, you might be saying, "Why would I pay 5 dollars for a game that I can beat in an hour?" and that is where you are wrong. You may think that game is straightforward but it is a brutal experience that is comparable to Dark Souls. Even IF you could beat in an hour, I advise to unlock all the characters which you could not definitely do within an hour. The Binding of Isaac has a euphonious soundtrack and unique artstyle to accompany you along your quest to destroy Mom.
Tl;dr The Binding of Isaac is an AMAZING game that is very ADDICTING. You should pick up at the Steam store especially for the low cost of FIVE DOLLARS!

Just.... Stunning... This game is so simplistic, yet so vast. Buggy and miscalculated yet so cohesively well forged. I can't honestly say I have so easily made a purchase. I mean, the game is 79 pence, I even bought it for a friend. You aren't losing much by buying this if you don't like it but I would be surprised if you don't. The game features many gamemodes and 3 classes which all suit a certain playstyle depending on what kind of player you are. Personally I favour the medic class, I mean currently I have 7 and a bit hours on this game and I have apparently spent a whole hour healing. There is something for everyone and the amount of mayhem makes the game indescribably fun. The main gamemode people tend to play is survival or conquest where you have to defend a generator while surviving hordes of dinos as well as bosses and also capuring objectives. When you capture an objective, vehicles spawn which you can use until they blow up ( can be repaired using utility gun or medic gun with engineer perk). There are not many thing that are more fun than sitting in a tank and blowing up a T-Rex in about 4 hits, or using gattling guns on mechs or helis or the back or cars. Although the gamemode shares the same objective most times, it doesn't get boring. You'll find every game you find yourself in different situations  and dilemmas. The big dinosaurs (bosses) add more challenge to the game as they are significantly harder to kill while also having certain abilities like chomp( 1 hit kill without perk) or charge which often involves kiting hordes and juggling the dinos between the players. You may have noticed I mentioned perks earlier, another feat in this game that makes it so fun to play is the sheer amount of perks and weapons you can buy at the end of each round. This allows you to really customise and adjust the way you play and invest in the game, this also makes the game fun to replay because you can change your playstyle depending on what you have bought. Weapons are less crucial because you can survive the entirety of the game using a pistol although it is a bit harder, there are still fun weapons like LMG's, SMG's, Turrets and gatling guns which are hella fun to mow down hordes with as well as more ...  majestic weapons like the ion blade or the energy carbine.  This game is honestly worth picking up with friends, it's only 79 pence and provides so much value for money. There is just something special about it that allows so much fun with friends the aspect of working together to try and survive, although seen in other games, is a bit more effective and I can't put my finger on why... This game is honestly like a 9.5 out of 10 only because it has some bugs and there is not an option to turn off rain even though I kind of like it.
I genuinely enjoy this game, not only for it's very Tim Burton esque style, but for the brutal multiplayer survival experience.

There are some Pros and Cons of The Witcher 2 for new players to evaluate before considering buying it or not:
-Pros:

After the hours I put in, I suppose I should something about this game.
Watching the trailer at the end of screenshot list above is quite funny to me. I imagine this was a trailer made before release when things weren't final, but some things in there are pretty bad. Especially Iorveth's voice makes me cringe. The current Enhanced Edition still has pretty good graphics, sound and music. Even today. But the most important thing with a game like this is still story and gameplay.
The story is the absolute star of this game. The game makes you a part of it in a way that far too few games do. Of course you need to be open to having a lot of dialogue to listen to, stuff to read and choices to make. If you do, then you will be presented with multiple possible viewpoints of the story based on pretty hard and morally grey choices. Some of which keep you wondering if you didn't make a big mistake.
Gameplay is good, but not perfect. It takes quite some time to get used to it. The tutorial of the game gives you a few pointers and then throws you into a fight that you will most likely fail at. With an "easy" recommendation as a result. I played on "hard" instead because I wanted to force myself to learn to handle the various aspects of combat better. For the most part, combat works well. It is based on the idea that taking damage is a bad idea (unless you play on easy maybe). Especially early in the game you need to watch out and attack with care. But even later in the game overconfidence can kill you very quickly. But you have quite a few options for how to approach combat based on choices you make in the skill tree (and you only get enough skill points for about a third of the available skills). After you get used to it, it works very nicely. The only thing that I had occasional problems with is that you can't break off attacks. Once you click for an attack, you're committed even if you immediately realise it is a bad idea.
Technically the game has issues though. I played the Linux/SteamOS version, so this may be specific, but I had about a dozen crashes. Also a few instances of the interface not responding to the mouse anymore, forcing me to restart the game. A little annoying, but it couldn't deter me from discovering everything the game had to offer.
Highly recommended!

This is the game that hooked me on the Total War series.
This game is damn well near perfect. Sure it has a few bugs, but the game has been out since 2006 you can easily find a mod to fix any unresolved bugs or gameplay issues. And speaking of mods, Medieval II: Total War has the best overhaul mods I've ever seen, let alone played. Sadly buying the game on Steam complicates modding since there is no Steam Workshop for the game. For instance my favorite overhaul mod, Third Age: Total War (a Tolkien-inspired mod), refuses to launch no matter what I do.
As for the game itself, I cannot praise it enough. While not eye-candy like Shogun II or Rome II, the gameplay (both in campaign and in battle) was the best of the original Total War games. After Medieval II, Creative Assembly begins a gameplay transformation that peaks in Rome II. Essentially this game perfects what CA started in their previous games (Rome, Shogun and Medieval).
The question is ultimately: Should I buy it? Well there's a free demo, but the Gold Edition (or rather the Medieval II: Total War Collection) is worth full price. I'm not sure I have the right words to describe it, but "yes, more Total War please" will suffice.

For me it's one of the best strategy games I've ever played. It has the 'one more turn syndrome - except there are no turns'. It has deep and demanding strategic system, but is also quite intuitive and easy to comprehend. The multiplayer with its option to continue alone/join somebody by overtaiking the AI is superb. People whine about some minor issues or the mid game boredom... On the other hand they seem to ignore the fact, that most games have late/end game boredom - where you know that you've won already but must 'click it to the end'... Here you don't have such problem, coz after a short comfortably boring period - which still can be surprising at times - when you are powerful enough to feel secure - there comes the end game crisis - absolutely ingenious in its simplicity. Don't get me wrong - I'm a casual player, not a guy with a miniature Tiger Tank behind his bed and 5000h in Europa Universalis or such... And Stellaris is perfect for me. It gives me times when I feel like a hardcore strategist, but it doesn't overwhelm me with charts, spreadsheets and statistics. Perfect.

SUPERHOT: MIND CONTROL DELETE is a standalone Superhot game based around the original game. This time, instead of having a proper story mode with like, being trapped in the game using a VR headset, they are runs. The game still withholds the original SUPERHOT mechanics that we all know and love and that still make us Badasses.

Runs mean that you can choose a certain mode. Each mode contains a different trait. The trait in addict is Hotswitch. The others, I do not want to spoil for you all :)  The first one is addict. It is about a girl so addicted to the game that she is uploading her mind to the system. To make that happen, you need to decrypt the code of the game and you run into a few issues. To decrypt some bits, you need to play the game. And you do have HP. You start off with very limited amount (2hp). This means if you get hit, you get another chance in life but use it wisely. One death and you're out. Every 2 rounds you get an oppurtunity to get an extra heart or get a complete refill. My advice is that you use an extra heart if you only get hit once. Getting an extra heart will give you an extra hp and that will be filled. It's like regenerating the one you lost. If you get hit more than once, and you're above 2hp as your maximum, just feel free to refill completely before you die!
After selecting a mode (i.e Addict), you're on a screen with Easy and the rest decrypted. After completing easy, you will have access to medium and more. The higher you go up, the more chance of the runs increasing, I have not yet reached past medium at the time of this review. As i said, I do not want to spoil it for you. . The gameplay is 50/50 same old. Yes. You still have to kill a certain amount of enemies. Yes there are levels. No there is no full story. But there are runs.
I personally really like this game and recommend it to everyone. If your reaction speed isn't great, I would not recommend this as it's hell. Enemies can come out of spawn points just if 1 enemy dies and others are still alive. It is unpredictable and you could get killed unless you're fast. For an early access game this is great and it's totally a buy now instead of waiting.

Pope dies of old age. Archbishop of Milan is voted as Pope. Milan is not anymore excommunicated and is now loved by Pope. Papal state declares war against me and allies with Milan and Venice. I then send Emperor Henry the Crusader and his crusader army (the ones that conquered Cairo and Alexandria). Some years after Emperor Henry the Crusader lands outside of Rome and attacks the Pope himself. Emperor Henry the Crusader kills the Pope with his crusader army.

Outside in the real world it’s grey, moody and depressing. Fear not, because here comes The Night of the Rabbit.
The Night of the Rabbit is a colorful point and click game with a dark twist. The game delivers on the artwork and overall visuals, but the story is also very entertaining. As the game progresses it becomes more clear that everything isn’t always what it seems to be at first sight.
The soundtrack fits the game with overly sweet songs mixed with more strange and epic ones.
Even years later I still enjoy the soundtrack from time to time and it always takes me back to some of the games locations.
The atmosphere in Mousewood and the surroundings is relaxing and can easily give you a warm feel at times. Still there is always this sense of ‘something is off’ and it is this sensation that helps to build up the total feel for the game.
The puzzles aren’t always very logical and can get frustrating without looking it up, but for me the advantages of the game vastly outweigh this point.
The minigame with cards is also very fun to play and you’ll want to go on until you get all the cards!
All in all this game is one of my favorite point and click games especially at times when your mood can use a boost. Also, if you have a partner this game is perfectly suited to play together while you hang out on the couch in front of the big screen on a rainy Sunday. Highly recommend it!
Really fun! I would definately recommend this game to anyone!

Especially since a lot of moves involve an animation which takes a second or two to complete and can't be interrupted, so if the game things you pressed a button you have to sit and wait until it hands back control...by which time you'll probably be dead. The final boss is completely "trial and error" and the only way to pass is to learn from your mistakes - unless you're psychic you're not going to know what you should be doing.
Oh,
Oh, and the game WHOLLY and COMPLETELY rips off Limbo. You'd swear you were playing a level pack for that game. There is NO way Monochroma would exist without Limbo. The monochrome outlook, small boy lost in a big world with unknown assailants chasing him (when they remember to, although that was more from INSIDE), factories where you have to navigate cranes and cogs, "rising water" levels involving moving crates to the right place so you can float on them...elevator navigation where you climb up and around them to move around, constant rain to give the whole place an oppressive feel...frankly I'm amazed there isn't a "gravity reversal" section or a giant spider.
Gah. The game as a whole plays very well but the complete lack of originality really lets it down. It just feels like a Limbo fan-project or something. And £14.99 is FAR too expensive.

This one has a special place in my heart.
Yeah, sure, it all starts of with a really pretty main character.
You end up entangled in tales of humanity though, so don't think for a second, you get away unscathed.
As a game, this offers sublime action combat, switching from 3D to various versions of isometric and 2D locks.
It switches from action combat to shoot-em up to twin-stick shooter variations.
And then there's fishing and role-playing.
There have been games with more depth, but this is hardly the focus here.
The complexity, skill needed and fun to be had all follows the immersion needed.
I can't remember any game where I thoroughly lost any connection to reality so fast.
But that probably comes from the story, it's characters and the questions it's asking.
Don't be fooled by the beautiful world, it's cruel.
But you already knew that ...NieR kinda has a reputation for that.
I don't think the story is about existentialism or philosophical questions, as many have claimed.
those are just means of transporting a far more important issue.
There would be spoilers up ahead, so I'll leave you hanging here.
Just know this much: if you approach it with an open mind...
...you will forget how beautiful this world is.
...you will be surprised how fun it is to have a partner.
...you will understand that it actually has to end like this.
In short, this game will help you grow as a human being.
Short update: I might add, that I'm using a PlayStation 4 Controller.
As far as I've read, Keyboard & Mouse are not really worth trying (I only used the mouse for giggles with pod).
But that's fine by me, it shines the way it is designed.
I strongly disagree to have any of the suggested possibilities for KBM integrated, as it would influence gameplay in various ways.
The game is done well with all the options available for customization and switches back and forth between KBM/gamepad like no other game I've played.
I had no technical issues throughout the game (except the somewhat frequent slow downs), although I only use a GTX 750, which doesn't even pass the minimum requirements.
There have been a lot of players who ran into problems though.
Let me add another thing. Easy Mode. It's actually most brilliant. It has customization within the games mechanics. If you'd wish to, the only thing you'd need to do was moving to where you want to go. Even dodging/attacking could be done automatically. While some see that as an invitation to use one hand for something entirely different, it actually breaks with something, that devides videogames from any other medium: You usually can't get the whole story, if you're not capable to kill the last boss.
It basically includes the "movie edition" into the game. It's actually quite a remarkable feature, especially for people like me, who opted to go for movie editions on various occasions (such as the original Drakengard, Odins Sphere, Final Fantasy XII) because of a lack of time, or just interest in the condensed story, or not wanting to collect every last weapon for some bonus. It's a sublime feature (although I opted in for the great combat this time, I might go for an Easy Mode run to learn the japanese Version, so I can concentrate on understanding).

Lamia's Game Room is an Old maid card game remade into single-player game with story told in visual novel style. For those who don't know the rules - there is every card twice in the deck, except one, Lamia. Players take one card from opponent and match pairs of cards in hand until only the Lamia is in hand of any player - and that player loses.
In real life, this game revolves a lot around bluffing (
) so even there is a sort of bluffing - as you can do specific emotions when opponents are picking a card from your hand. Every opponent will react differently to your emotions, some will get confused because of your grinning, some because of you'll be telling them to draw quickly.
The game, considering the low pricetag, has a nice artworks, especially for the cards. Sadly, if you are going to be playing the English version (which I assume), expect a terrible translation from original Japanese version. There are many typing errors and sentences that feel weird - it's sad that developers didn't pay a proper translator, I think it could justify increase of price to two euros.
With bad translation interest in the story goes off, and then there's just the repeating card game that's fun for one or two times, but not fun to play ten games in a row. Even though it's a cheap game and it has nice artworks, I don't think at all it could be worth recommending.

In a few words, this game is amazing.
Fun Hack n' Slash gameplay with tight controls, very difficult and unforgiving game, mainly so in the prologue, I don't recommend starting it on hard, it's a game that, unless you're used to the genre you should start in Normal or easier, if you're absolutely incompetent, don't worry, the game can be very accessive by enabling chips that basically play the game for you.
The story, though, now that's the thing, this game has 5 true endings, unlike other games you don't start the game all the way over to get the different endings, each and every play through is truly different from the previous one, either by introducing a different playable character or more story elements, so if you're afraid of getting burned out by starting a new game+, don't be, try it out first, it's a whole new thing.
This game can be very depressing, be it via the main story or it's side quests. Sometimes it will throw you something that gives you hope, but most of the time, it will try to crush you, make you question your existence and objectives and I love it. This game said something that I've always thought about, it connected to me in a very deep level, so I hanged on, 'till the very last true ending, ending E...
...that ending really gives you hope to keep on, no matter how hard it gets.
Oh, and to the person who I gave up all my time and effort to help! Life can be quite the ♥♥♥♥♥, it might be meaningless and you will suffer a lot, but so what? Memory wasn't made for us to remember or good times, it's there so we don't repeat our mistakes. Suffering and hardship makes us stronger, if we can get past it!
Time is only wasted if you think it is, when you do the things you love, that isn't wasted time, nah, that's called 'time well spent'.
So struggle, scream, cry and fight, even if it's all really meaningless and futile, because isn't it fun, to hang on to this tiny hope, to deny when life it says to give up, to fight the impossible?
I know I love it and I wouldn't have it any other way, so hang on, I'm here with you, even if you think you're alone.

Summary: This game has more potential than US high school students do. It needs some polish, but the core is there.
The good:
*The core mechanic of Superhot is still just as amazing as it always has been
*I have yet to find an unfair fight, though they are all very challenging so far.
*The combination of soft-permadeath and multi-level-per-checkpoint design works well.
*The increased durability you gain over time meshes well with the new roguelike format.
*More types of weapons and objects to swing, shoot, and toss than I remember from the original.
The bad:
*Level variety is lacking as of yet- Every level feels like it is one of 3 or 4 levels.
*Lack of a replay feature as of yet.
*Some UI elements, such as the directional marker reticule for swords, are not in yet.
My suggestions to the dev (Level Gen):
*Try to convert level bits to a tileset with attachment points and very small tiles.
*Make the tiles attach to only certain other tiles.
*Have positions that objects can spawn from a list on, be they usable, decoration, or both.
*Add elements like activatable objects that open walls temporarily, and use them to create monster closets.
*Make the monster closets from the above idea activate on their own shortly after enemies spawn, spilling foes out.
Other suggestions to the dev:
*Add a replay feature, and possibly tie shared replays to steam workshop and allow anyone to view anyone's replay?
*Re-integrate UI elements from Superhot into Mind Control Delete, such as a line or arrow swing arc for melee weapons.
*Offer more optional minds and more options for between-level progression.
*Add a practice mode with customizable difficulty via enemy spawns and weapon placement, perhaps?
As a player I see this game going ahead swimmingly, weather you take my suggestions into account or find your own ways to deal with the flaws remaining in this game and add yet more content.

Wow, Gearbox. I take back almost everything I said about Borderlands 2 and the Pre-Sequel, before I played the latter title. BL2 struck me as very very derivative of the first game and way too impressed with itself -- I mean, it worked as a business idea, the game sold a ton. But I really thought Gearbox was creatively bankrupt after playing most of BL2 a while back, and never planned to get the Pre-Seq.
But holy crap, I was wrong. The Pre-Seq is BY FAR the best in the series IMO. They added some ridiculously fun mechanics with the O2 tanks, some very clever (and slightly annoying, but mostly clever) altitude-based environment puzzles, and the LASERS, man. The lasers are FUN. SO much fun. The characters' skills are way way better than 2's -- Athena is my girl all the way, although I also dig Nisha's gunslinger skills. Wilhelm is a pretty amusing character, and I dunno about the robot. Don't care, honestly, but I do plan to fiddle with him at some point. Actually, I'm so glad they finally regulated him to a much more secondary role, because I don't know about you, but that "ha ha I'm an annoying sidekick" joke was running damned thin.
And they actually wrote a -- so far -- rather decent story that isn't 75% pop-culture jokes, and they manage to give some of the characters some personality, AND the level design & art design blow me completely away. The writing: as much as I love Anthony Burch, the comedy in BL2 got super old after you ran around Pandora for the tenth time, and there's only so much "look at me I made an internet joke" I can take, honestly. The Pre-Seq actually puts forth a fairly interesting story and the comedy is mostly derived from the characters and who/what they are, not all the quotes they can spout at you. And that is a HUGE leg up in my opinion.
I still get frustratingly lost in some of the environments and the map still sucks, but wow. I'm kind of in love with this one.

Received for free due to being a SUPERHOT Kickstarter backer.
In it's current state, the game doesn't have much to it. A couple of classes, 3 difficulty levels, no story, with no progress or level carried between playthroughs. There's only ~10 areas, and there's no new weapons / guns, although there are new throwable props. For now, there's absolutely no reason to purchase this over SUPERHOT, especially as SUPERHOT's post-game modified modes are pretty much the same experience, with more progression and challenge.
However, the game's framework has extremely high potential. Semi-randomised SUPERHOT levels, with a persistent life count between them, is addictive. If pulled off correctly, this could be a rogue-like spin on SUPERHOT with even more addictive gameplay than the original.

This game was... magical, pun intended. It felt slower-paced than many other puzzle games I've played, which could be good or bad depending on what you're in the mood for.
The music, voice acting, and especially the backgrounds were superb; the characters were distinctive and most were well-developed. And effin' loveable.
The plot was interesting and didn't dip into as many cliches as it could have. I also liked how the story was set in and around one area, instead of moving linearly from place to place, set of puzzles to set of puzzles--it felt nicely centered.
The puzzles were mostly fair; there were a few places where something was either badly laid out or just odd, but for the most part everything went smoothly. I did end up using a walkthrough for the second part, have to admit.
The ending... wow. It tied everything up with a minimum of deus ex machina, explained all the little things that hadn't made sense to me over the course of the game, and gave nice closure with room for a sequel (Matt Kempke, if you're reading this, the reception in Germany doesn't matter; there's a lot of us who would love sequels). Plus, dat twist!
A solid 9.5/10 (just needed a bit more help on some of the puzzles than the game provided). Play this game!

People need to stop comparing this to Hotline Miami; it has significant overlap with Metal Gear Solid just as well.
The story is decent, it's not absolute trash and doesn't do some stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t like Hotline Miami or Metal Gear Solid (I'm sticking with comparing it to MGS btw). But the voice actors are sub-par; I'm supposed to believe you're actually a gruff detective, not be able to tell that you're actually a 20-something trying your hardest to sound gruff. The script is trying just as hard as the actors are at times, but ♥♥♥♥ that let's get to the game itself:
It's a 2D over-the-top perspective 'kill everyone on the map' title, and that's where comparisons with Hotline Miami end. You don't have firearms or a vast array of weaponry, it's just your knife. The people you're attacking won't start firing bullets all over the place and you don't have to run around the map incredibly fast whilst avoiding gunfire. On the contrary, you move at walking speed and the map is just one screen, with environmental traps strewn about and a man that will often times show up at the level and hand you some sort of useful tool (smoke bomb, stun bomb, change of clothes to evade police, etc).
This is where the Metal Gear Solid comparisons begin. Your objective is to kill everyone in each level, of which there are around 12 total (some bonus levels are unlocked later). You can't just go around killing everything, though. If you kill someone in the open, others will notice and call the cops. You can kill them before they get to a phone, but if you kill THEM in front of others then everyone will be alerted. It's in your best interest to kill off people in secluded areas of the map, getting rid of the bodies in dumpsters and potholes. Just like MGS, you have to stealth your way to your kill, but unlike MGS you can freely walk about in the open as long as people don't take note of your misdeeds.
Just like in MGS, you can evade your would-be captors. If a body is discovered, the police are alerted and wrap the body in tarp, leaving right after. If someone saw you murder the person (and you can't kill them before they snitch) and tells the officer, you can run from the cop. Here's the thing though: you move slower than the cop, and running tires you out incredibly fast (you gotta stand still to recharge your run meter), so you gotta either be far from the cop when the chase begins or use the level's (limited) traps against the cop, killing him and evading capture. The cop will come as often as people call him up.
What's annoying, though, is that other than the cop there's no other penalty for murdering out in the open. Now, murdering people in the open is an unrealistic tactic (other than the Casino level), since you'll get caught by the cop. The crowd will also beat your♥♥♥♥♥unconscious (7 or so seconds) if there's 10 witnesses, which is plenty of time for the cop to arrest you. But if you do manage to escape a few times (totally doable), the crowd doesn't flinch. I wished they would run from you, automatically call the cops when they saw you, or you automatically failed the level if you scared the crowd from the scene by openly comitting murders multiple times. Or even just once, there's no reason people should see you kill someone and not run when they see you again. If only one person saw you commit the act, there should be a penalty whereby they start telling others,  beginning a timer whereby you have to murder them before word gets too far out.
My wishes for the game aside, another gripe I have is the lack of options in murder. There are traps throughout the level, but they generally come down to four: spike the punch (people around the bowl will be poisoned), rig electronics (people in front of it will automatically set it off and die from the explosion), cut an item down so it lands on someone, or push someone into/onto their deaths (off a rooftop, onto a saw machine). Otherwise the majority of the level is spent waiting near areas to dispose of bodies, carrying sleeping bodies to secluded areas to murder them, and running from place to place to get a kill or two. Levels can take well over 20 minutes too, so you either love the satisfaction with finishing a level with no cop alarms or hate how tedious it might get. The fun comes in noticing a huge crowd and getting pick offs as people walk to other rooms, then piling bodies in areas and running back and forth to get kills whilst killing people that noticed the bodies. You either look for openings to take the bodies to a disposal site or you love the thrill of being found out.
Party Hard is a fairly novel idea that holds promise for further development in game mechanics. It's sort of like the difference between MGS1 and MGS3; they added so much that MGS1 looks archaic by comparison (and it is). It's definitely a game deserving of a sequel or some sort of continuation of the groundwork laid here. It doesn't overstay its welcome, and provides just enough material for a playthrough to be satisfactory and fresh. I'd wish they worked on a few more mechanics and implemented things, otherwise I'll give it a big thumbs up because it's still new enough without said mechanics to be enjoyable.

WARNING: This game is broken! I suggest you wait for the next update (in about 10 or so years).
There are a few gameplay-breaking bugs in the game as well as minor annoyances that make you regret buying this game as it is now. I'll list just some of them so you can judge for yourself.
- Double-spawning entities that cause various physical systems to break down and to stop functioning including doors, fans, conveyor belts, etc. This is extremely obnoxious.
- Turrets do not work in both crossfire and stalkyard.
- Hitboxes are misaligned with the playermodel.
- The nuke can be spammed in crossfire, resulting in multiple instant deaths until it stops.
- Acid pool trap does not do any damage in Snarkpit.
- Bad interpretation of client actions by the server, resulting in delayed crossbow fire, gluon beam redirect, tau laser, etc. (this can be altered somewhat at a large cost of server resources).
- Team deathmatch does not function entirely correctly.
- Coop is broken (yes there is a coop command).
- Extremely bright lights due to HDR rendering and the use of mostly quadratic lighting and huge glow sprites.
- Strange looking gloss on weapons.
- Weapons feel "clunky" compared to the original game.
- Changing playermodels in the menu does not work (can be changed via console though).
So that's that. If you're still edging towards buying this game, you're not making the biggest mistake of your life since the remaining community is awesome and sometimes hilarious.
P.S. The Tau Cannon is glorious!

An incredibly fun, minimalistic bullet-hell rhythm game, that I had a ton of fun playing around with. The levels in this game all feel natural and everything that fires at you fires at the right time. Think of Beat Hazard but with actual structure to it. Nothing about this game feels out of place and everything flows naturally.
The level editor, coupled with the tutorials from the developer himself, are very simple to grasp and use. And with the community making so many pretty good levels, there's plenty of content that this game provides. The auto-generated levels are not so good, as it's not even close to being as deep as the core levels are, basing more on the loudness of the track over any indtrumentation going on.
And of course, the soundtrack is great too! It has songs that I've had on since I bought the game and listen to regurlarly. The songs fit the game perfectly with their instrumentation and melodies and provide an amazing look when paired with the visuals.
In my short time with this game, I've had tons of fun with it. Everything is easy to grapple with and incredibly fun, I definitely recommend it for rhythm game fans.

Disclosure: Got a free key due to being a early backer for the original SUPERHOT.
I loved the orignal one and this expension (I believe free on release for prior owners, check storepage to be sure) doesn't seem to differ much from that.
What used to be mods (different modifications you could use while playing) are now implemented into the "minds". You now play a mind which has certain mods to keeps the gameplay fresh. Also the minds arent a bunch of lose levels but are a mission you begin at 0% and try to get a 100% without dying, you die you start at 0%.
Big difference from the first SUPERHOT is that you now have "lives" of which you start of with 2 and can get through progressing the mission up to 4 of (as of this moment, it's early access so this still can change). The lives basically lets you get hit without instant death. Does this make it easier? Yes for a single level, but your lives count like classic platformers over the entire mission. So you still need to watch out for those bullets.
My early verdict is, much of the same goodness I loved in SUPERHOT. So a thumbs up from me.
As of the moment of this review this is still an early access product, please bare this in mind.

This is game is sort of an odd one, but I loved it.  A slow, seemingly child-aimed point and click adventure game opens up to a bit more wonderous story with some great depth in lore and setting, but like an origin story it ends before it can really get into that enticing depth.
The story follows one Jeremy Hazelnut as he finds himself whisked away on a wizard apprenticeship in some alternate dimensions.  As stated above, it opens a bit slow but a bit less than halfway through the game the background and world building that has gone into the game begins to show itself.  The puzzles are occasionally a bit confusing as is always the case in P&C games, but as the game goes on that problem pops up much less often.  My only real grip with the puzzles is that as you progress you learn spells as part of your apprenticeship, but you end up barely using them for the importance it is presented with in the story.  German voice acting is robust and enjoyable, and some of the music is downright amazing (although sadly not on the soundtrack).  The ending of the story opens up a much deeper setting that sadly this game does not get into exploring, but if Daedelic ever makes a sequel I am very much looking forward to seeing more of the story.
The game comes with some some audio stories collected as you play the game that add a bit to the world building.  While they are relevant content, unfortunately they can be a bit... difficult to listen to.  Listen to the one with the deer who can't sleep, and pass on the rest.
Game performed flawlessly, no audio or performance glitches.  I played about 14 hours (minus one or two for listening to the audio stories and away).  I really enjoyed myself, its one of the better P&C adventure games I've played.  I'd recommend it.

I can't believe that I didn't stumble upon this game sooner. Very interesting concept. You play as a guy who's just trying to get some sleep, but your neighbors are throwing a party. Your goal is to kill everyone at the party without getting arrested or killed. While you'd think that a game with such a premise would be completely tasteless and without merit, I have to say that the simple graphics and the generally comedic tone keep you from taking things too seriously. My only real gripe is that most of the game play mechanics seem to be somewhat unnecessary, although I suppose that mastering them may allow you to proceed through the game more quickly.

This is not a great game. It might not even be a very good game. In terms of the amount of gameplay that you get, it's certainly not worth the regular price (€19.99 at time of writing). But if you can find it on a good sale or in a bundle, it's also worth your time.
Where
succeeds, and even excels, is in the substance of the world it has created. The dark, dystopian, and, yes, monochromatic visuals create a repressive, threatening environment that is enhanced by the sparse but moody and atmospheric soundtrack. The environments have a solidness and a weight that add to a repressive sense of danger as you progress on your journey from deserted cornfields to run-down city streets to gritty industrial factories and on into a frighteningly hostile high-tech future filled with the sleazy, unchecked power of old-school capitalistic robber barons. (Did I mention that this is also a political game?)
While the environments and atmosphere are exceptionally crafted, gameplay is simply adequate, with fairly standard puzzle-platforming elements. Some puzzles are likely to be familiar to those with a lot of experience in the genre, but overall the challenge level is adequate. Dying resets you to an automatically saved checkpoint, with a blackout in between that is just long enough to make you not want to die too often. And while the different environments are very well distinguished from each other, they're not all that long: a full run-through of the game can be done in less than 2 hours once you're familiar with the puzzles.
One thing that
will not give you is a lot of information. The world you're running through feels vast compared to you, and none of it is explained for you. Hints are revealed throughout, especially towards the endgame, but it's entirely up to the player to make sense of some very strange things.
Overall, this is not an enthusiastic recommendation for the game at its full price, but the combination of artwork and atmosphere make this a worthwhile experience if you can find it cheap.

this game is pretty hard to review, mainly because it's always better to just play these type of games yourself to see if you're into it.
but if you like listenening to music and trying to not suck at bullet hells, then you won't regret getting this game.
however, make sure you have a good computer, because flash.
alright, let's start off with the positive points:
+ this game has an awesome OST, the default level are really well made AND the DLC levels are just as good if not better (and they're free!)
+ this game has a slow-motion mechanic, which I personaly never think about using, but when you remember to use it, it can really help you
+ the community is, in my opinion, one of the best out there: friendly, fun and helpful.
on top of that, Soundodger+ probably has my favorite level editor, it's really simple but it allows you to do so much when you wrap your head around it (which only takes about 2 hours, that's how simple it is)
now, for the negative points:
- this game has bugs, mainly with the editor, but nothing too big, as a simple restart will fix them.
- if you work on a level in the editor for too long, the game seems to slow down, as if something isn't being unloaded, which forces you to restart the game.
- as with many other flash games, this game does not run well on low end computers at all.
to sum this review up, this game will be a great addition to your library if you like music, bullet hells and making levels.
Final Rating: 8/10

I'm really wanted to recommend this game. I really like some aspects of it.
++ The music is really good, to the point that I actually left the game open to listen to it while doing other things.
+ About the first third of the game was good. The characters interacted well, the story was good, the jokes were alright (not personally my cup of tea, but fine), and the little investigation puzzles you did were a rather nifty.
There were also things I personally liked, but I think some people would be mixed on.
+/- While I personally was not bothered with it, I can see some people really not liking the art in this game. The backgrounds are perfectly fine, but those characters. It's a generic animu style, complete with nonsensical proportions and bad shading.
+/- The game also has some animations, which I find is another mixed point. The also has that animu style, except now instead of being poorly shaded, it has wonky physics and for some reason has Japanese voice acting. The Japanese is handwaved in game, but that doesn't make less odd. While it is rather cool that the developer included these scenes, I would have been perfectly fine with them being left out.
+/- Another mixed point in this game is the player's input within the story. Your actions in the game don't change anything about the ending, they only change which character/s you end up with. However, to make up for this, the game has several puzzles, each increasing in difficulty. While I found the puzzles a nice tradeoff, I can see people really not liking the lack of player induced change. Also, while almost all of the puzzles were good, I found the very last puzzle more tedious then challenging.
There was even something that, while I personally didn't like it, I could see someone else liking it.
-/+ The CGs in the game I did not like at all. They, for me, crossed that line from being animu but fine to looking like DeviantArt trash. Proportions were completely off, to the point that Max's spine looked broken in most of them. Sometimes the characters in the CG looks little to nothing like the characters that are meant to be in them. However, if you can look past those two things, then they are rather nicely detailed, colored, and shaded.
However, there was one thing that made this game unbearable.
or about 1/3 of the way through the game, the entire thing became completely unenjoyable. I enjoyed this part the game so little that everything wrong with the game at that point was a major issue.
- What happened to the humor? It turned from a mix of deadpan, referential jokes with a mild hit of random/stupid humor to being
random and stupid with the occasional deadpan joke thrown in. This got to the point where there is an entire sequence where the only thing going on and the only joke occurring is that Max thinks that a cardboard cutout is really a person. Why did you do this? I at least found the first part's humor harmless. Now I just want to hit all of the characters (well, mainly Max).
-
- Because of the two points above, all of the characters are ruined, as they do basically nothing else.
- The entire story is also frequently derailed due to this.
- The ending contains a not really twist that I predicted.
- The very ending contains a stupid joke they decided to make an animation for because...reasons.
Due to the latter portion of the story, I cannot recommend this game. The good parts are mostly ruined by the bad. If you can get the game for ten dollars or less, then it might be worth it, but even that's a stretch.

Firstly, I'd recommend it for fans of hack & slash gameplay. However, it has several issues with the PC port. It's got a hard time with widescreen monitors. The resolution scaling is totally off! Setting it to fullscreen actually shrinks the game's screen and distorts the text, as if stretching a lower resolution. I needed a MOD to get it to run in proper fullscreen. Using that mod, I don't have a mouse cursor in the game... at all. Using the windowed mode doesn't let me adjust the size of the window, so I can only see about 1/3 of the game. The keybindings can be awkward since this game was designed for the PS4. There is no dodge button, nor can you bind it to a key. If I equip the taunt module for 2B and 9S, I can't use it using a keyboard. The "flight" sections of the game are awkward with a mouse and keyboard. If you play for long periods, it will begin to stutter more often, at least for my rig. I've had about 7 crashes so far. Most, if not all, crashes were due to using the steam overlay or alt-tabbing. Other than that, it runs mostly well. Though, with an i7 4790k, 16Gb of DDR3 RAM, about 4 TB of storage, and a GTX 980ti, I really should not be dropping FPS with this game's graphical fidelity.
Onto subjective things: The melee combat, music, and story are all well done! The "flight" sections of the game are basically galaga sections or similar types of games. Combining that with the epic music and an epic setting TOTALLY destroyed my immersion. It's like putting nerf guns into the fight scenes of serious war movies. I would have liked them to do what games like Black Ops 3 did with their flight sections. They were simplified because the main focus is obviously infantry combat, but it did not destroy my immersion. I wasn't going to expect Ace Combat, nor should anyone. The big slow-moving jpeg bubbles of damage definitely didn't help with the immersion either. Sure, fire enough and it'll get very difficult to avoid being hit, but geez how did humanity lose to an army that uses bubble-blowers as their primary ranged weapon? Not to mention they can be destroyed by shooting them with bullets or smacking them with melee weapons. The machines are derpy-looking except for the bosses (thankfully). I do appreciate the effort that went into the story as well as the easter-egg types of endings and nostalgia-like gameplay segments, like with the hacking minigame (except for the "flight" sections). It makes sense why 9S is a young boy. (It's a stereotype) The graphics are... pretty bad. I wasn't going to expect Crysis or Battlefield, but geeeeeez they make half-life 2 look like a graphical masterpiece in 2017. The animations are thankfully well done, except for lip-syncing.
It may sound like I expect too much from games, but this is a $60 release. It has to compare to other $60 games. It comes up short in too many areas to justify recommending it at its current price. This is a $50 game at maximum! $45 would be good. It's like selling a beat-up used car with a good sound system at the same price as a brand new car of the same model. If The Witcher 3's devs could do it, so could these devs. Now THAT is a game deserving of the $60 price!

It's a cute visual novel. I use that term advisedly, because that's what it is. It's not a game, per se. It's a story with a set beginning and a largely concrete end. There are puzzles, and objectives, but it's only a question of doing them well or doing them poorly. You can't skip them.
So, what's here that's worth your time? The art is quite good. I understand it may not be to everyone's tastes, but I enjoyed the artistic direction of the project. The writing is excellent, though slightly slapdash at parts. The animation, when there is animation, is top notch. The characters are strong and well-defined, except when they aren't, which is usually for the sake of humor.
There is one gag towards the end that relies both on the static animation and the fact you probably haven't given a particular character much thought that I thought quickly redeemed whatever flaws there were here, so I'm certainly pleased. It's a fast game, if you let it be. You could easily get sucked into the writing and spend hours at each decision point, trying to obtain more of it.
Now, a few words about the... let's say content, might not go amiss here. Yes, it involves a full-scale magical sex change. Two, in fact. The story, insofar as it takes a stance, could also be described as sex positive. There's a great deal of sexual content and innuendo. Outright nudity? That I didn't see, though that's not to say it's not there. You can tell at a glance  up therewhat the usual 'level' might be.
Soundtrack is... basic? Very basic? It seems to be largely stock music, and it was probably the weakest part of the game for me. Since there's no speaking outside of the animated sequences, you could easily play with the speakers off and your own music on. I'm not going to recommend that, but it's something you could do.

I was able laugh at the TG (initials for transgender) elements in the game (it's meant to be funny I swear, they use that joke more than once), able to respect the other modified ladies in the game (bunny girl, fish girl, etc), and I was able to get into the story that was given.  It takes place in Australia and has a rather funny plot about drug investigations, magical forces, elemental people and other crazy stuff of that nature.  It also has a feature in which you can hook-up the main character (who recently went from male to female) with characters in the story through certain decisions (you have a police man, a lesbian otaku, a bookworm, a redhead and a mystery man), and has some fun (albeit repetitive) investigation sections as to spice up the visual novel and overall have you do more.  In summary, it's very weird, should never be played in public, and is very anime at the end of the day.  Seriously though, keep this game hidden from people, you will be judged harshly for playing this.

I think the thing that bothered me most about this game was that you break your brothers leg and have to carry him around, and you can only put him down in spots that are well lit because you are a nice guy - that part is okay, I guess, but it falls apart when you can only leave him under a street lamp in the rain where you're going to lower a shipping container (which will crush him if you're not quick enough to pick him up after you pull the lever), but you aren't allowed to put him down next to the lever that lowers the container which is not only well lit, but it's also out of the rain and not under threat of being crushed. The puzzle plaforming just doesn't seem well thought out in some spots, which will probably cause me not to bother coming back to this, which is a shame because it looked so interesting.

The one word that came to mind that perfectly describes this could-have-been-a-gem of a game's inexcusably dumb design decisions is inane. No not insane, inane. There are some more maps after you beat the game but after I tried the first extra map I had finally had enough. The game is extremely inconsistent in several ways. Overall it has so many nonsensical game flaws that you would think whoever made this was in special needs classes in school. I wanted to like this game pretty bad because it looks and plays awesome, but ultimately it is just not even worth the $6 I spent on it on sale. When it was over I breathed a sigh of relief and looked forward to forgetting the developer's constantly glaring bad mistakes that I experienced the whole time that put a sad sheet over how awesome the game could have been.
+ Awesome graphics/effects
+ Mass murder simulator
+ 80's theme-ish
+ Fun traps
+ Fun gameplay
+ Works great with xbox 360 controller
+ Very fun for a few levels
- Only a few traps per level, sometimes as few as one or two.
- Most traps have a very tiny kill radius or are gone after someone walks into them once.
- Immediately turns into a stabfest. Out of the 40-50 kills needed per level, you will have to get 40+ of them by stabbing. For the first few levels I didn't care and was having a blast. After that, it got real old real fast because all levels are just tedious, long, drawn out stabfests.
- Killing people means just stabbing, waiting for a cop or medic (who for some stupid reason wear tall white chef hats) to come and cover them up and leave, then stab some more, move around to not get caught or linked to a kill, and that is all there is to the game really.
- FBI agents will sometimes start running after you even though they had no way of linking you to any murders.
- Cops will bust you without proof you killed someone, just because you are standing in their walk path (can be avoided with practice).
- Bouncers will attack you at first site even if you just started the level and just walked close to one. Why? Why me when I am just a party goer like everyone else? Are they psychic and know I will start killing people? Is there a secret APB out to all bouncers to stomp to death anyone fitting your description?
- Bouncers stomp you to death when they catch you. Why?
- The campus party has bouncers. Why? What campus party has ever had bouncers? Let alone the four to six that are on that level. Ignoring the fact that it is insanely stupid to have bouncers at a campus party in the game, why have so many?
- Sometimes you get linked to the murder just because... well just because the game felt like it.
- The music is sub-par at best, and it got so mind jarringly repetitive that I very quickly couldn't stand it and played 95% of the game with my headphones around my neck. The problem is that when you retry a level 20+ times and have to hear the same one-tone one-beat music restart every time you retry, it makes you hate it quickly.
7/10 for a few levels
5/10 otherwise
5.5/10

SuperHOT... superHOT... OK I'll give up.

If you really like British 'twee', you might enjoy this game immensely. If not, you'll probably just find it annoying.
One tip for early on in the game: There is a stick to the left of a circle of mushrooms. Clearly it's something you want to pick up because it's obvious that you need a stick to get to other items in the area, but the activation shape for the stick is only a few pixels wide and not actually on the stick, but rather a smidge down and right from the left end. I ended up having to read a cheatsheet to figure out why I couldn't make anything work, only to find that the stick was indeed required. A bit of very careful moving of the mouse around the stick revealed the tiny activation shape. This bug might be specific to the Mac version.

I feel like the roguelike elements for this game didn't add a lot- in fact, they often detracted from the experience.
In the original Superhot, one of the coolest things was attempting cool, flashy maneuvers without knowing for certain if they will work- but that's fine, if it doesn't work you're just back at the start of the level, no big deal.
The rogue-like progression elements strongly discourage that sort of experimentation, in favor of the same, safe set of two or three tactics deployed over and over again.
It still gets a recommendation, because hey, more Superhot, and it's still a good game by the general standard, but I don't think the rogue-like elements were a good design choice.

Even though it looks like it's just another boob VN, Max's Big Bust actually has a nice amount of content in its bosom. There are a few parts where you actually get to do what can be loosely considered police work, talking to suspects and doing goofy Phoenix Wright-style hijinks to catch criminals, there's a poor imitation of a pet raising game on your phone, and there's even random trivia games placed everywhere they could fit one. The story is pretty good, and the budget seems higher than most similar games, including having a few animated cutscenes (though it seems like they were animated by a Japanese studio, so the dialogue is in unsubtitled Japanese explained in-game by a joke, but the dialogue isn't that important in the scenes that have it) and subjectively good art - most of the art is pretty well-drawn, and the characters who have questionable poses or designs get mocked by the other characters pretty often so it feels more like the game is laughing with you. One route of the game took me 15 hours to finish, and I doubt the other romance paths will take as long but that's still a pretty good length for an Australian VN to me.

MonoChroma is a puzzle-platforming, adventure game set in a dystopian world, somewhat similar to the 1927 movie, Metropolis. Coincidentally, MonoChroma also utilises silent narrative, is black and white (except for a splashing of red here and there) and portrays a city ruled over by an assumed evil mega-corporation. Unlike Metropolis, the story is full of plot holes and explains nothing. It’s supposed to be set in an alternate 1950’s. But even this is unclear. The backgrounds and world you move through actually have some strong design and a unique art style, really pushing for that dystopian mood. But that’s it. Because there is no reinforcement from the story, no exposition or even purposeful and strong characters, the setting becomes weak and shallow.
I feel that MonoChroma is a loose collection of similarly themed pictures that has been converted to a game, after the developers played Limbo and decided that indie fans love this stuff.
Here is  an exert from the blurb with my opinion interdispersed throughout:
The game is a cinematic puzzle platformer that balances unique puzzles
and non-violent action
. Take on the role of a boy who needs tp carry his injured little brother on his back
. You can’t move as quickly or jump as high with him on your back, so at times you have to put him down…
MonoChroma has been described as Limbo meets Ico
; but it’s much more than a skilled mix of two great games
: It is a deeply visual, intellectual, and emotional experience
. Explore the hard emotional realties of life
, relying on interactivity to grow into an art form
.

Alright, as a good friend of mine would say, this one is done and dusted. It took me around 4 hours to finish, although those of you who are platformer stars could finish this in 2 hours most likely.
It is a beautiful game in the spirit of games like Limbo. Mostly black and white and grey, but with red highlighting special things and used to accent the striking world portrayed. Simply put, this game is stunning.
The game is also fairly deep into the topics of slavery and forced labor, by way of an alien invasion kidnapping all the children. You and your brother try to evade capture in this crazy adventure. There is a bit of surrealism or what have you here as well. You leave home to play, and really never see your home again. The ending is one of hope and sacrifice.
The controls for the gamepad handle quite nicely. I had no issues with clipping or any of the other issues that can plague games. In fact, as far as I could tell, it was perfectly optimized and free of bugs.
It has a nice save system that auto saves at each juncture or before any challenging or significant event and also saves after getting past the same. That means that when you die (and you will likely die a lot), you never have to go too far back, and so even with the more challenging sections, it never feels like a chore.
Speaking of challenges, this game was quite challenging IMO. Not that everything was, but I found that some of the puzzles could stretch the mind trying to find the solution. Still, with a 4 hour playtime, obviously nothing was insurmountable. In fact, I would say it was just right for the type of game that it is.
All in all, this one is an easy recommendation.

The one word that came to mind that perfectly describes this could-have-been-a-gem of a game's inexcusably dumb design decisions is inane. No not insane, inane. There are some more maps after you beat the game but after I tried the first extra map I had finally had enough. The game is extremely inconsistent in several ways. Overall it has so many nonsensical game flaws that you would think whoever made this was in special needs classes in school. I wanted to like this game pretty bad because it looks and plays awesome, but ultimately it is just not even worth the $6 I spent on it on sale. When it was over I breathed a sigh of relief and looked forward to forgetting the developer's constantly glaring bad mistakes that I experienced the whole time that put a sad sheet over how awesome the game could have been.
+ Awesome graphics/effects
+ Mass murder simulator
+ 80's theme-ish
+ Fun traps
+ Fun gameplay
+ Works great with xbox 360 controller
+ Very fun for a few levels
- Only a few traps per level, sometimes as few as one or two.
- Most traps have a very tiny kill radius or are gone after someone walks into them once.
- Immediately turns into a stabfest. Out of the 40-50 kills needed per level, you will have to get 40+ of them by stabbing. For the first few levels I didn't care and was having a blast. After that, it got real old real fast because all levels are just tedious, long, drawn out stabfests.
- Killing people means just stabbing, waiting for a cop or medic (who for some stupid reason wear tall white chef hats) to come and cover them up and leave, then stab some more, move around to not get caught or linked to a kill, and that is all there is to the game really.
- FBI agents will sometimes start running after you even though they had no way of linking you to any murders.
- Cops will bust you without proof you killed someone, just because you are standing in their walk path (can be avoided with practice).
- Bouncers will attack you at first site even if you just started the level and just walked close to one. Why? Why me when I am just a party goer like everyone else? Are they psychic and know I will start killing people? Is there a secret APB out to all bouncers to stomp to death anyone fitting your description?
- Bouncers stomp you to death when they catch you. Why?
- The campus party has bouncers. Why? What campus party has ever had bouncers? Let alone the four to six that are on that level. Ignoring the fact that it is insanely stupid to have bouncers at a campus party in the game, why have so many?
- Sometimes you get linked to the murder just because... well just because the game felt like it.
- The music is sub-par at best, and it got so mind jarringly repetitive that I very quickly couldn't stand it and played 95% of the game with my headphones around my neck. The problem is that when you retry a level 20+ times and have to hear the same one-tone one-beat music restart every time you retry, it makes you hate it quickly.
7/10 for a few levels
5/10 otherwise

Firstly, I'd recommend it for fans of hack & slash gameplay. However, it has several issues with the PC port. It's got a hard time with widescreen monitors. The resolution scaling is totally off! Setting it to fullscreen actually shrinks the game's screen and distorts the text, as if stretching a lower resolution. I needed a MOD to get it to run in proper fullscreen. Using that mod, I don't have a mouse cursor in the game... at all. Using the windowed mode doesn't let me adjust the size of the window, so I can only see about 1/3 of the game. The keybindings can be awkward since this game was designed for the PS4. There is no dodge button, nor can you bind it to a key. If I equip the taunt module for 2B and 9S, I can't use it using a keyboard. The "flight" sections of the game are awkward with a mouse and keyboard. If you play for long periods, it will begin to stutter more often, at least for my rig. I've had about 7 crashes so far. Most, if not all, crashes were due to using the steam overlay or alt-tabbing. Other than that, it runs mostly well. Though, with an i7 4790k, 16Gb of DDR3 RAM, about 4 TB of storage, and a GTX 980ti, I really should not be dropping FPS with this game's graphical fidelity.
Onto subjective things: The melee combat, music, and story are all well done! The "flight" sections of the game are basically galaga sections or similar types of games. Combining that with the epic music and an epic setting TOTALLY destroyed my immersion. It's like putting nerf guns into the fight scenes of serious war movies. I would have liked them to do what games like Black Ops 3 did with their flight sections. They were simplified because the main focus is obviously infantry combat, but it did not destroy my immersion. I wasn't going to expect Ace Combat, nor should anyone. The big slow-moving jpeg bubbles of damage definitely didn't help with the immersion either. Sure, fire enough and it'll get very difficult to avoid being hit, but geez how did humanity lose to an army that uses bubble-blowers as their primary ranged weapon? Not to mention they can be destroyed by shooting them with bullets or smacking them with melee weapons. The machines are derpy-looking except for the bosses (thankfully). I do appreciate the effort that went into the story as well as the easter-egg types of endings and nostalgia-like gameplay segments, like with the hacking minigame (except for the "flight" sections). It makes sense why 9S is a young boy. (It's a stereotype) The graphics are... pretty bad. I wasn't going to expect Crysis or Battlefield, but geeeeeez they make half-life 2 look like a graphical masterpiece in 2017. The animations are thankfully well done, except for lip-syncing.
It may sound like I expect too much from games, but this is a $60 release. It has to compare to other $60 games. It comes up short in too many areas to justify recommending it at its current price. This is a $50 game at maximum! $45 would be good. It's like selling a beat-up used car with a good sound system at the same price as a brand new car of the same model. If The Witcher 3's devs could do it, so could these devs. Now THAT is a game deserving of the $60 price!

A pretty fun game for what is a simple concept; kill everyone on screen.  Use environmental traps, hide bodies, outrun the cops and move around each level in full sight, but hidden.  It's a great concept and I think the graphics, music and simple controls really make it a fun experience.  At first I assumed it was similar to Hotline Miami ans in some minor ways it is, but it's certainly not as frantic and the real similarity is in visual style and music...not in gameplay.
The story isn't very interesting at all, but the gameplay is pretty much spot on and it's a very addictive and fun game.  It's rarely cheap and if you fail a level then it's usually due to some mistake you have made.  Most of the time this mistake is not taking your time and trying to kill someone at the wrong time. I was guilty of this often, though you want "just one more turn" until you get that satisfaction when you complete a level.
There's potential for replayability with the ability to use different characters, each having their own particular skill.  Unfortunately the repetitive gameplay means that going back to do it all again with other characters can seem a bit pointless.  Playing through the entire story is good enough and it doesn't really need 20 hours of content.
After failure, the level is randomised.  This means you cannot learn the layout of a level and practice to perfect it.  This could be a bad thing for some players, but it actually adds to the challenge.  I never found the random levels I was given to be either too easy or too hard.  They are all challenging in their own way.
Party Hard is a nice take on the stealth genre and is a nice change of pace.  There's perhaps not enough content to justify a full price purchase.  Get it on sale and you will have enough to entertain you for a dozen hours or so.  Nice gameplay, fitting music and enough of a challenge without being ridiculously frustrating.

The “worst game of all time” has evolved into a new beast.
Four years ago TREK Industries released its first iteration of Orion: Prelude to abysmal reviews. The space-aged dinosaur hunter was broken and a mess.
But TREK did not abandon its title. It revamped it with numerous free updates and dropped the price to an expectation-free dollar. Last year TREK released a new trailer for the game, poking fun at its past with the “worst game” quote and followed with multiple reviews from big-name outlets slamming the release.
Critics have since been far more favorable to the updated game.
It’s not perfect — far from it. It’s still wonky and a little shallow. But the reworked game now works. You can travel to different terrains and fight hordes of dinosaurs with different weapons. You chose from the general artillery — pistol, shotgun, assault rifle and sniper. You also get the choice of three different classes, although the jet-pack boosted option is an easy, advantageous choice.
You fight dinosaurs small and large, including tyrannosaurus and spinosaurus. They come  across 10 waves of attacks, with each wave getting more intense and featuring more big dinos. You can complete the quests in both single player and multiplayer modes.
Orion: Prelude also features more than 270 achievements in case you feel like hunting more than just dinosaurs. While the game is far from a premiere first person shooter, it’s a lot of fun and is a testament to how developers can salvage a dream.

Party Hard:
~~~~~~~~~

Inspector John West has seen and hunted down plenty of criminals during his time but nothing could prepare him for the streak of killings like this! A party killer who has marked him forever!
Party Hard is an action/stealth/ strategy game were you are playing an insomniac psychopath (at the start of the game and you will be able to play others during the course of the game) who has had enough of loud parties. Armed with a knife, you will join and disrupt 19 parties across the great U.S. of A! In each party, you will be able to use some objects and make deadly traps out of them and hopefully wipe out a large number of partygoers. Look around for suitcases, they have items that could be very useful for your killing spree: smoke grenades, which are great to conceal yourself while ravaging the party; stun grenades, which are helpful for a short time; dynamite, which needs to be placed in the right spot to be effective, but will trigger the SWAT team to come around.
If you can’t find any suitcases, look out for the guy with a black coat and hat - he always has great goodies (another insomniac, I guess)! Make sure nobody sees you doing your grim business or the police will be on your tail and escaping is not that easy! Random events can help you too, you might be lucky and a bear can jump into the middle of a party and ransack it for you! A bit like a Spanish toreador, just watch and enjoy!
I really like the randomization in this game, each time you restart a party objects might not be in the same place as your last attempt, and they might not be there at all. Which gives this game a good re-playability. It is a challenging game and it will take you several efforts to ruin a party to death!
Nice pixel graphics with a funky audio! I really enjoy the pixel art through the story too. You can either use the keyboard or a gamepad for the control. I personally prefer the gamepad. I reckon it is easier.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Partially randomize levels
-	Nice pixel graphics and great audio
-	Fun and easy to play
-	Trading cards and achievements
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Challenging at times
Partying too hard can be deadly indeed but this time you will be the executor!

Why should you get soundodger?
Well, I think you should get it because the game is fun, good music, variety in said music, starts easy, but you'll soon realise that this game is not a cakewalk, the community is generally pretty good and there's an editor. The editor is mainly the reason why this game got so much replayability. Would I have put currently nearing 400 hours in it if it wasn't for the editor? no I wouldn't.
I can't stop you from reading the negative reviews, however, I think most of them don't say correct things, so keep that in mind. You like editors? You like difficult games? You like relaxing games? with the editor and custom levels, there's bound to be stuff for you, lots of it. You can literally use any music you like, not even copyrights can stop you there.
I guess the only real question would be whether you like rhythm games and bullet hells in general.
For most people, I think this would be a game you could easily get into, so why not give it a shot? perhaps this is the game you've been looking for that you can just put tons of hours into.
The game is also a bit broken, sure, that's not enough to make me not enjoy the game, but it is really annoying when they do happen. There's lots of bugs, and it feels like Bean, the developer just doesn't care anymore. On top of that, the game doesn't have the best performance, this is because the game is made in flash.
